title: The linear vertex of a flat normal-cone fibre survives every minimal-prime quotient
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring containing $\mathbf Q$, and suppose $R$ has no nonzero nilpotent elements [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal, put $A=R/I$, $k=R/\mathfrak m$, and $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Assume $G$ is flat over $A$, meaning that tensoring injections of $A$-modules with $G$ preserves injectivity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $B$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], let $e\ge0$, and fix a graded $k$-algebra isomorphism
$$\theta:G\otimes_A k\xrightarrow{\sim}B[T_1,\ldots,T_e],\quad \deg T_i=1$$
[def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\epsilon:B[T_1,\ldots,T_e]\twoheadrightarrow k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$ be the quotient by $B_+=\bigoplus_{j>0}B_j$. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime), put $\bar I=(I+\mathfrak p)/\mathfrak p$ and let
$$q_{\mathfrak p}:G\otimes_A k\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\bar I}(R/\mathfrak p)\otimes_A k$$
be the canonical graded quotient map. Then
$$\ker q_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\ker(\epsilon\circ\theta).$$
Equivalently, the quotient $\epsilon\circ\theta$ factors through $q_{\mathfrak p}$ as a surjective graded map onto $k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]$.

source.place: Agent-written filtered-algebra synthesis for the ILO VIII 2.3.13 synchronization input. Supporting algebra: Tag 00IP, lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero (separated I-adic filtration); Tag 00MH, lemma-free-fibre-flat-free (finite flat modules over a local ring are free); Tag 00EW, lemma-reduced-ring-sub-product-fields, part (3) (minimal-prime elements are zero divisors). None of these tags alone states this polynomial-vertex assertion.

proof.text: Fix a minimal prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$; it is contained in $\mathfrak m$. Put $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/I\subset A$ and $F=G\otimes_Ak$. On degree $j$, the elementary quotient-tensor identification $M\otimes_A(A/\mathfrak n)=M/\mathfrak nM$ gives $F_j=I^j/(I^{j+1}+\mathfrak mI^j)=I^j/\mathfrak mI^j$, since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. The target of $q_{\mathfrak p}$ in degree $j$ is $(I^j+\mathfrak p)/(\mathfrak mI^j+\mathfrak p)$. Here $\bar I^{j+1}$ disappears because it lies in $\mathfrak m\bar I^j$. Consequently every $h\in(\ker q_{\mathfrak p})_j$ has a representative $a\in I^j\cap\mathfrak p$: if a representative $x\in I^j$ has $x=b+a$ with $b\in\mathfrak mI^j$, $a\in\mathfrak p$, then $a=x-b\in I^j$. The quotient-tensor identification used here sends $m\otimes\bar c$ to $cm$ modulo $\mathfrak nM$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$; bilinearity verifies both compositions.

source.place: Agent quotient calculation from the associated-graded definition and the tensor universal property; no flatness of R/p is asserted.

proof.text: Both $q_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\epsilon\theta$ preserve degree. Therefore it suffices to prove the kernel inclusion on homogeneous elements: decompose any kernel element into its finitely many homogeneous components. Degree zero of $q_{\mathfrak p}$ is the identity $k\to k$ by the preceding formula. If $e=0$, $k[T_1,\ldots,T_e]=k$ has no positive degrees, so the inclusion already follows. Otherwise suppose for contradiction that a homogeneous $h\in(\ker q_{\mathfrak p})_n$ has $H=\epsilon\theta(h)\ne0$. Then $n>0$ and $e>0$. Choose its representative $a\in I^n\cap\mathfrak p$ as above, and write $\alpha=a\bmod I^{n+1}\in G_n$. Its reduction in $F_n$ is $h$.

source.place: Agent homogeneous reduction, including the degree-zero and e=0 cases.

proof.text: The residue field $k$ contains $\mathbf Q$: a nonzero rational is a unit in $R$ and has nonzero residue. Thus $k$ is infinite. Apply [lem-trf-graded-polynomial-vertex-regularity] to $f=\theta(h)$, which is homogeneous of degree $n>0$, with $e>0$ and $\epsilon(f)=H\ne0$. Multiplication by $f$ is injective; the isomorphism $\theta$ therefore makes multiplication by $h$ injective on $F$.

source.place: Agent-written algebraic refinement of the item, former steps 5--6. Supporting Tag 07BV, lemma-colimit-syntomic (monic polynomial regularity in its proof). Infinite-field direction input: existing lem-trf-infinite-field-top-form-direction; no Stacks tag asserts this full graded-polynomial comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-graded-fibre-regular-lift] to the given $R,I,n,a$. Its flatness hypothesis is assumed in the item, and its residue initial form is exactly $h$. It follows that $a$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R$.

source.place: Agent-written filtered-algebra synthesis of the item, former steps 1--2 and 7--8. Supporting Tag 00NZ, lemma-finite-flat-local; the finite-free case of Tag 00ME, lemma-mod-injective; Tag 00IP, lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero, or Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module (2). These tags supply the local module inputs, not the full filtered statement.

proof.text: But $a\in\mathfrak p$ and $R$ is reduced. The statement [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-zerodivisors-union-minimal-primes] therefore gives a $b\ne0$ with $ab=0$. This contradicts the preceding step, so $\epsilon\theta(h)=0$ for every homogeneous $h\in\ker q_{\mathfrak p}$. The homogeneous reduction proves $\ker q_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\ker(\epsilon\theta)$ for every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$.

For the equivalent formulation, define the descended map on a class $q_{\mathfrak p}(x)$ by $\epsilon\theta(x)$. The kernel inclusion makes this well defined; addition, multiplication and grading follow from those of the original maps. It is surjective because $\epsilon\theta$ is surjective, and its composite with $q_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\epsilon\theta$ by construction.

lean.note: The tensor factors are reversed by the canonical symmetry. The component target is its canonical quotient presentation by the initial classes of I^n intersect p; the degree-n quotient is (I^n+p)/(m I^n+p), exactly the special fibre of gr_(I mod p)(R/p). The vertex target is B_0[T], identified with k[T] by the standard grading. Its map is the actual degree-zero projection on coefficients. These concrete models introduce no hypotheses or choices.
